explanation: To achieve perfect forwarding within a C++14 generic lambda (`[](auto&& param)`), the type used to instantiate `std::forward` must correctly capture the lvalue/rvalue nature of the argument. This is achieved by passing `decltype(param)` to `std::forward`. This ensures that if an lvalue is passed, an lvalue reference is forwarded (copying), and if an rvalue is passed, an rvalue reference is forwarded (moving), regardless of the complexity introduced by the universal reference parameter deduction.
practical_example: A developer creates a generic wrapper lambda to apply a normalization function before calling the final function `func`. By using `decltype(param)` with `std::forward`, they guarantee that large, temporary objects passed to the wrapper are moved efficiently instead of being copied unnecessarily.
keywords: Perfect Forwarding Lambda, Generic Lambda Forwarding, decltype std::forward, Universal Reference Forwarding
chapter: Item 33: Use decltype on auto&& parameters to std::forward them
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
